a: GET retrieves data. Should not change server state. Safe and idempotent.
POST creates a resource or triggers an action. Body usually carries JSON data.
PUT replaces a resource at a known URL. Often idempotent.
PATCH partially updates a resource.
DELETE removes a resource.
201 Created means a new resource was successfully created.
204 No Content means success with an empty body (common for DELETE).
400 Bad Request means the client sent invalid input.
401 Unauthorized means authentication is missing or invalid.
409 Conflict means the request clashes with current server state (e.g. duplicate).
422 Unprocessable Entity often means validation failed.
502 Bad Gateway means a proxy/upstream server returned an invalid response.
503 Service Unavailable means the server is temporarily overloaded or down.
Authorization: Bearer <token> is a common way to send API keys or JWTs.
Pagination returns data in pages (limit/offset or cursor) so large lists stay fast.
A webhook is an HTTP callback your server receives when an external event happens.
Clients send a unique key so retries of the same POST do not create duplicates.
OpenAPI (Swagger) describes REST APIs so tools can generate docs and clients.
gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework using HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers.
SOAP is an older XML-based web service protocol; most new APIs prefer REST or gRPC.
